extracted.intended_audience: academic journal peer reviewers (potential and current reviewers for Taylor & Francis and similar journals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers on deciding whether to accept a review, how to assess manuscripts (originality, methods, presentation, fit), how to make a recommendation (accept/revise/reject), and how to write constructive comments for authors and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review (refereeing) is a collaborative process where manuscripts are evaluated and commented upon by independent experts in the same field to provide feedback to authors and allow editors to assess suitability for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains purpose and value: helps authors improve work, allows editors to assess suitability, maintains journal quality; acknowledges limitations and criticisms of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to review
rubrics_metrics.description: Motivations for reviewing include helping authors improve papers, maintaining rigorous peer review, staying aware of current research, building relationships with editors, and gaining professional prestige.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also frames reviewing as a conversation among author, reviewer, and editor; highlights reviewer role in identifying gaps in references and suggesting relevant literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check journal review model before accepting
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm what form of review the journal operates (single/blind/open) before agreeing to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps the reviewer understand anonymity expectations and how to compose feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm review submission format
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the review must be submitted via a structured form or as free text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing the format helps you plan the structure and level of detail of your report and ensures you complete required fields (e.g., specific review questions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat review materials as confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers and correspondence sent to reviewers are privileged confidential documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share manuscript contents or communications; maintain confidentiality throughout and after the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare conflicts of interest promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: If a conflict of interest exists, make the editor aware of this as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts can preclude reviewing or require disclosure; informing the editor early helps preserve the integrity of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept only if you can meet time and expertise requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Only agree to review if you can complete the level of review required in the allotted time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If time is short, request an extension or offer a briefer report; if unable, inform the editor early so they can find alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate the journal and Instructions for Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Visit the journal homepage to understand published content and house style; refer to the Instructions for Authors to see if the paper meets submission criteria (length, scope, presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding journal scope and house style helps judge suitability and provide relevant guidance to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete review questions or report form
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the journal's review questions or report form to indicate the relative strengths or weaknesses of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer structured questions honestly and use them as the backbone of your assessment; include free-text comments where possible to justify ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect author opinions supported by evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A referee may disagree with the author's opinions, but should allow them to stand provided they are consistent with the available evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reject or criticize novel interpretations solely because they differ from your view; focus on evidence and argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide positive feedback as well as constructive criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors welcome positive feedback in addition to constructive criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance critiques with acknowledgment of strengths to guide authors and avoid discouraging them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess originality and novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether the submission is original, relevant and novel and whether it contains significant additional material beyond what is already published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider contribution to the field and how the work builds on or departs from existing literature; flag overlap or duplicate publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess topicality and cutting-edge nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the research is cutting edge or topical and whether it helps to expand or further research in this subject area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider current debates and the paper's timeliness to the journal readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess contribution relative to author's prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the paper significantly builds on the author’s previous work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for incremental vs. substantive advancement; request clarification or additional comparison when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess fit to journal scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether the paper fits the scope of the journal and whether it would be of interest to the readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not a fit, consider recommending the author reconsider the paper for a related or alternative journal or another form (e.g., shortened article).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend alternative outlets or formats when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the paper should be shortened and reconsidered in another form or submitted to a different journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific suggestions on alternative venues or formats when the paper's content or length does not suit the current journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate abstract and concluding section
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether there is an abstract or brief summary of the work and whether the paper includes a concluding section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the abstract adequately summarizes key findings/approach and that conclusions are supported by results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess completeness and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether the paper is complete (has required sections) and whether the structure supports reader comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for missing elements, unclear organization, or sections that need reworking to be coherent and complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess language quality (Standard English)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the submission is in Standard English to aid reader understanding; recommend an English editing service for non-native speakers where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not the reviewer's job to copy-edit the entire manuscript, but correcting wording where technical meaning is unclear is helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess methodology and analysis accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the methodology presented and any analysis provided are accurate and properly conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for appropriate methods, statistical rigor, reproducibility, and whether conclusions follow from the data and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess significance and potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the significance and potential impact of the paper are high or low.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge likelihood of influencing practice, policy, or future research; indicate reasons for the expected impact level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for supporting data, citations, and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure all relevant accompanying data, citations, or references are provided by the author to give adequate context for the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag missing citations, suggest additional literature, and note whether data availability is sufficient for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider length relative to contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the content of a paper is of sufficient interest to justify its length; each paper should be as short as needed to contain all useful and relevant information, and no longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recommending shortening, indicate specific areas where truncation or condensation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess presentation: writing, tables, graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether the writing style is clear and appropriate to the readership and whether tables/graphics are clear and labeled appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend improvements in clarity, figure/table labeling, and overall presentation where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate references for adequacy and currency
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the paper contains appropriate referencing to provide adequate context and whether it is well integrated and up to date with the existing body of literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest missing key works, note over-reliance on outdated sources, and recommend strengthening literature integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation categories and criteria (Accept/Minor/Major/Reject)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall recommendation to the editor: Accept (suitable as is), Minor revision (ready after light revisions), Major revision (needs substantial changes), or Reject (not suitable or requires fundamental changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending revisions, list specific changes; for major revision, indicate substantive areas such as expanded analysis or literature review; for rejection, explain why revisions would be too fundamental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed, author-facing comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide comments suitable for transmission to authors that seek clarification on unclear points and offer elaboration and suggestions to improve clarity, succinctness, and overall quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific (avoid vague statements), highlight strengths and weaknesses, give concrete examples and instructions for improvement, and indicate whether the paper's subject justifies its length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and constructive criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Be critical whilst remaining sensitive: construct comments carefully so the author fully understands what actions to take to improve the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid generalized or vague statements and negative comments that are not relevant or constructive; use sample phrasings as models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role regarding English/language editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are not required to edit the paper for English, but it is helpful to correct English where technical meaning is unclear and to suggest professional editing where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend language editing services for non-native speakers when language issues impede comprehension or mask substantive issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess likely citability and scholarly interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the paper is likely to be of sufficient interest to be cited by other researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on novelty, utility to the field, and whether the work fills a recognized gap to support predictions about citation potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess robustness of methods, analysis, and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether methods, analysis, and conclusions are robust and of a high standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out methodological weaknesses, suggest additional analyses or controls, and flag unsupported conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review revised manuscripts and list of changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When authors revise a paper, reviewers are asked to affirm whether the revisions have been carried out satisfactorily; authors should submit a list of changes and comments for transmission to reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare revised manuscript to the list of changes; confirm if required items are addressed or request further clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: If unable to review, inform editor and suggest alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are unable to review a paper, inform the editorial office as soon as possible and, if possible, recommend an alternative expert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notification prevents delays in the refereeing procedure; if deadlines will be missed, inform the office early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make editors aware of any potential conflicts of interest during review
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify editors of any potential conflicts that may affect your ability to review impartially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts may require recusal or disclosure; early communication allows editors to manage the review appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sample phrasings and examples to frame feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ suggested sample comments to help phrase positive feedback, constructive criticism, or language suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include positive praise for writing and contribution, targeted comments for substantive deficiencies, and specific linguistic alteration suggestions; tailor language to the manuscript and journal.
